reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its given compatible normed additive-group structure. Let n be a natural number with n > 0 and dim_R(E) = n + 1. Write S = {z in E : ||z|| = 1}, with the subspace topology and the n-dimensional sphere atlas specified in the input: its charts are the stereographic charts stereographic′ n v, and the chart chosen at z is stereographic′ n (-z). Its model is the identity model with corners on R^n = EuclideanSpace R (Fin n).

Let i : S -> E denote inclusion. For z in S and v in the model tangent space T_z S, use the extended tangent norm N_z(v) = ||d i_z(v)||_e, where d i_z is the vector-valued manifold derivative of inclusion and ||.||_e is the ambient extended norm. Thus the tangent norm is specified by the inclusion derivative, rather than being left as an arbitrary tangent-norm parameter.

For x,y in S, define d_R(x,y) in [0,+infinity] as follows. Take all continuous paths gamma : [0,1] -> S with gamma(0)=x and gamma(1)=y that are C^1 as maps from the unit interval with its indicated one-dimensional half-space model to the sphere model. For each such path, take the nonnegative Lebesgue integral over the unit interval of N_{gamma(t)}((d gamma)_t(1)); the 1 is the unit tangent vector in the parameter direction. Then d_R(x,y) is the infimum of these lengths in the extended nonnegative reals. Equivalently, its integrand is ||d i_{gamma(t)}((d gamma)_t(1))||_e. The infimum over an empty admissible family has the extended-real value +infinity.

For every x,y in S, the theorem asserts
  d_R(x,y) = ENNReal.ofReal(arccos(<i(x),i(y)>_R)).
Here arccos is the principal real inverse cosine; the inner product of the two unit vectors is in [-1,1]. ENNReal.ofReal embeds a nonnegative real into the extended nonnegative reals (and sends a negative real to zero), so the right-hand side is the finite principal angle in [0,pi]. This is a global pointwise identity for every ordered pair of unit points, including equal and antipodal points, with no additional restriction on the pair.
scopes: Universal, global and pointwise on all pairs of the radius-one sphere in ambient dimension n+1 with n>=1. The length uses nonnegative integration on [0,1], and the admissible paths are C^1 in the manifold-with-corners sense on that interval, including its boundary. No almost-everywhere qualification applies to the asserted distance equality; there is no probability measure, stochastic process, asymptotic limit, rate or finite-horizon hypothesis in this theorem. It is not restricted to nearby points or pairs below the antipodal angle.
